title: Global derived Hom adjunction for coherent-space pushforward
statement:
Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived pushforward is computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and tensor pullback $Lh^*$ by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means the diagonal is quasi-compact. Write $R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(P,Q)=R\Gamma(Z,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Z}(P,Q))$ for global derived Hom, where internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and $R\Gamma$ is the right derived global-sections functor [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. If $Z$ is over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, regard this as an object of $D(A)$ by restriction of scalars. Its degree-$j$ cohomology is canonically $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Z)}(P,Q[j])$. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism with $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space. Choose a right adjoint $a_f$ of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, with counit $\epsilon_f$. For every $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the canonical counit-induced map is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$,
$$d_{P,F}:R\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,a_fF)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*P,F).$$
It is the map obtained by applying $Rf_*$ to the Hom arguments and then postcomposing with $\epsilon_{f,F}$. On degree-$j$ cohomology it sends $u:P\to a_fF[j]$ to $\epsilon_{f,F}[j]\circ Rf_*u$, using the canonical shift comparisons. No properness, flatness, boundedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_Y)$ be the canonical morphism of ringed topoi of $f$ [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]; its derived module direct image is $Rf_*$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-global-hom-direct-image] to this morphism of ringed topoi, with $A\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=A$ the identity, and to $K=P$, $L=a_fF$. That node requires no final objects and no site functor; this matters because $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ consists of schemes and has no final object when $X$ is not a scheme. Follow $c_{f;P,a_fF}$ by $R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*P,\epsilon_{f,F})$; call the composite $d_{P,F}$. The cited construction identifies this composite with global sections of equation-sheafy-trace, hence with the specified canonical map. Its natural cohomology identification gives $H^j(d_{P,F})(v)=\epsilon_{f,F}[j]\circ Rf_*v$, with the shift comparison inserted. This also establishes that the map is $A$-linear.

source.place: Tag 0E59 (lemma-iso-global-hom), equation-sheafy-trace; proof using the induced map on shifted Hom groups instead of the coherator test

proof.text: Set $T=Rf_*$ and $a=a_f$. The shift comparisons for $T$ are supplied by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], applied to the additive module direct-image functor. Fix $j\in\mathbf Z$. Shifting the source identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(P,aF[j])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(P[-j],aF)$. The supplied adjunction identifies the latter with $\operatorname{Hom}(T(P[-j]),F)$, and the shift comparison identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}(TP,F[j])$. The resulting bijection is precisely $v\mapsto\epsilon_F[j]\circ Tv$ from step 1. Explicitly, for $w:TP\to F[j]$, let $w^-:T(P[-j])\to F$ be its shifted form; the inverse sends $w$ to $(a(w^-)\circ\eta_{P[-j]})[j]$. The identities $\epsilon_{TQ}\circ T\eta_Q=1_{TQ}$ and $a\epsilon_F\circ\eta_{aF}=1_{aF}$, together with naturality of $\eta,\epsilon$, show that these maps are inverse. Thus $H^j(d_{P,F})$ is bijective for every integer $j$. All shifted objects remain in the stated full subcategories, since shifting merely reindexes quasi-coherent cohomology.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] in the abelian category of $A$-modules to the morphism $d_{P,F}\in D(A)$. Step 2 makes every cohomology map an isomorphism, so $d_{P,F}$ is an isomorphism. For $s:P'\to P$ and $t:F\to F'$, naturality of $c_f$ from step 1 and $t\circ\epsilon_F=\epsilon_{F'}\circ T(a(t))$ give
$$d_{P',F'}\circ R\operatorname{Hom}_X(s,a(t))=R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Ts,t)\circ d_{P,F}.$$
This proves naturality in both variables; the inverses are natural by composing this equation with the component inverses. The construction and argument never use properness, flatness, boundedness or Noetherianness.

The item statement matches 0E59 with Y=Spec A and is not weakened. The report is right that line 529 of the 0E59 proof is ill-typed. Steps 2-3 are sound: the shift chain Hom(P,aF[j])≅Hom(TP,F[j]) equals v↦ε[j]∘Tv, the explicit inverse works by the triangle identities, the cohomology criterion is applied in Mod(A), and naturality is correct. The new node is not a duplicate: lem-pc-sheaf-rhom-projection-formula and lem-sfb-direct-image-hom-open-ext are scheme-only, and lem-sfb-ringed-global-hom-cup-comparison targets the point topos. It also does not restate a clause of the item. One C-type fault: the new node required ringed sites with final objects and a final-preserving site functor u, and step 1 used 'Y/Y↦X/X'. But def-trf-algebraic-space defines X_et as schemes étale over X, so for a non-scheme X there is no final object and X×_Y V need not lie in X_et. The hypothesis fails exactly in the algebraic-space case. Repair: the new node is restated for any morphism of ringed topoi between small ringed sites. This is true by 0B6D (stated for ringed topoi) and by Leray via Γ(D,f_*E)=Hom(f^*O_D,E), as in the proof of 0D6H. Its A-action is now explicit through Γ(D,O_D)→Γ(C,O_C). Step 1 now takes the canonical ringed-topos morphism of f from lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model, which is added to uses, proof_deps and tool_uses as a generic construction; union of uses = proof_deps. Edge cases checked: X empty, P or F zero, f=id, A=0, negative j, non-scheme X.
